page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1.4xlarge is an x86_64 instance from the big data storage-focused instance family, operating on the KVM hypervisor. The virtual machine is configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs powered by 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processors and 64.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a 4:1 memory-to-core ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Network throughput is provisioned with a baseline bandwidth of 6 Gbps, and the configuration includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The defining architectural attribute of the ecs.d1.4xlarge is its massive bundled local storage capacity of 47244 GB backed by mechanical hard disk drives (HDD). It includes no GPU accelerators. This architecture provides exceptionally dense capacity for persistent and sequential disk-bound tasks, offering a very economical cost per gigabyte of local storage relative to solid-state alternatives.

The primary tradeoff of this instance stems from the mechanical nature of the local storage. While 47244 GB of HDD storage enables vast sequential write and read operations, random I/O latency and IOPS throughput are inherently lower than NVMe SSD configurations. Additionally, the Broadwell-generation Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processors provide standard baseline compute throughput without newer instruction extensions such as AVX-512.

Given this hardware profile, the ecs.d1.4xlarge is engineered for massive data warehousing, Hadoop distributed file system (HDFS) clusters, Apache Kafka log aggregation, batch data processing, and large-scale ETL pipelines that process massive datasets sequentially without requiring high random IOPS performance.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1.4xlarge is a dedicated big data server instance optimized for massive local storage capacity. Built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via the KVM hypervisor, the server provides 16 dedicated vCPUs from 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processors alongside 64.0 GB of system RAM, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB per vCPU allocation. The hardware profile is distinguished by 47244 GB of integrated local HDD storage and a 6 Gbps baseline network interface, without discrete GPU hardware. The dense mechanical storage array makes the instance highly cost-efficient on a per-gigabyte basis for storage-heavy workloads, balanced against the standard I/O latencies typical of mechanical disks. The ecs.d1.4xlarge is designed primarily for distributed big data frameworks, HDFS storage nodes, Apache Kafka clusters, batch data analysis, and large-scale data retention architectures.
